Community Response to Emergency Events 
 
The Community Directorate is working on an across-directorate basis to ensure 
Tipperary County Council has an effective and coordinated response plan for 
emergencies such as severe weather events. Guidelines in relation to 
Community Support Centres (CSCs) have been issued by the Department. 
Thirty-two (32) CSCs have been identified across the county to act as local hubs 
to support communities during emergency events.

Clonmel Woodlands for Health Project 
Sláintecare Healthy Communities is an active member of the multi-agency 
steering group overseeing the Clonmel Woodlands for Health project, working 
alongside Mental Health Ireland, HSE Mental Health Services, Tipperary Sports 
Partnership, Coillte, Social Prescribing and the Involvement Centre to coordinate 
planning, referrals, logistics and programme delivery. The project itself is a 
12-week guided woodland-walking programme designed to support adult mental 
health and wellbeing through structured, nature-based activity. As part of its 
contribution, Sláintecare is funding the transport required to ensure participants 
can access each weekly walk, and will also be attending a number of the walks 
to provide on-site support and maintain strong local authority involvement 
throughout the programme. 
 
Schools Cohort – Drugs Education programme 
The first pilot Drugs Education session for all Clonmel secondary schools will take 
place on 13 May 2026, with Gaelcholáiste TY students contributing peer-led 
project work. Delivered by Sláintecare Healthy Communities and key local 
partners, the session responds directly to the Clonmel Substance Misuse 
Research Report by providing clear information and launching a new QR code 
linking students to local supports. This pilot establishes the basis for a 
coordinated, long-term schools-based drugs education approach in Clonmel.

The three-day P2R Summit in Budapest brought together representation from the 100 
selected regions. Several high-level officials and representatives from the European 
Commission, European Investment Bank (EIB) European Committee of the Regions 
were also in attendance, and  joined the  panel discussions on the role of 
Pathways2Resilience within the wider EU Mission on Adaptation to Climate Change  
 
Above all, the P2R Summit was about connection, between the 1st and 2nd cohorts 
of regions. Over three days, all 100 regions took part in sessions and workshops 
reflecting on the work that 39 of the first cohort of regions have dedicated themselves 
to over the past 18 months.  
 
The 1st cohort shared both the opportunities and challenges of the journey, from 
developing their Action and Investment Plans to forging stronger relationships with 
local authorities, before passing the baton to the 2nd cohort on day three. It was a 
chance for our newly joined regions to draw inspiration as they embark on their own 
path towards climate resilience.

National Enterprise Week 
March 2nd to 6th was National Enterprise Week and a week packed full of 
business advice clinics, local media interviews and headline events were held 
across the county, culminating on Friday, March 6th with the final of the Student 
Enterprise awards in TUS, Thurles and the Questum Leadership, Enterprise and 
Innovation Summit 2026. Both of these events are outlined in separate 
paragraphs below and a summary of the weeks events are as follows: 
Business Advice clinics in the library, Clonmel; Civic Offices, Rosanna Road, 
Tipperary town; REACH, Roscrea; The Source Art Centre, Thurles; The Library, 
Nenagh and Carrick-on-Suir. 
A Digital Transformation & Artificial Intelligence (AI) for Small Business was 
held in the Abbey Court, Nenagh where founder of AI Ireland, Mark Kelly 
delivered a full morning, practical overview of how AI is being used for SMEs. 
Dr. John Cosgrave, TUS specialist on digitalisation for industry outlined some of 
the supports and research available to small business. Approximately 100 
attendees were present for this very interesting and timely workshop in the new 
world of AI that is shaping all our business and personal lives. 
‘The 30 day year proposition’ was the subject delivered by Pádraig O’Máille, one 
of Ireland’s freshest and writers on business and motivational issues. The 
proposition is a micro-learning programme designed to help business owners 
overcome poor execution and procrastination by reframing the year in 30 day 
cyles, to create sustained urgency and focused action. 
The Retail Edge was held at the Cashel Palace on the evening of the 5th of 
March, where a large attendance heard from retail experts, Padraig McMahon of 
Carraig Donn; Dr. Oran Doherty of Retail Ireland Skillnet and Peter Corkery, 
Digital Transformation Consultant. The experts guided a large attendance

The second panel was Hilary O’Shea of Otonomee, Orlaith Ryan of Shorla

and exit strategies for successful businesses was a hotly debated subject with 
the attendant audience of 180, drawn from Clonmel, County and region.  
Former Tanaiste, Simon Coveney, delivered the keynote address in between the

export trade and development. There was a very robust and engaging debate 
with the audience and Simon. Diversification across different political blocks
